name: Contract drafting and negotiation work product
one_line: J-DEPTH placeholder template for the INSTRUMENT-LEVEL record of getting ONE contract agreed on the practitioner side: the document-comparison or blackline header that names two source versions of the same instrument, the clause-keyed issues list with side-owned positions and open/closed status, the playbook whose columns encode preferred / fallback / walkaway positions against clause topics, the deviation-approval matrix for playbook exceptions, and the turn or circulation log that joins successive marked-up drafts. It is NOT activated by the words draft, redline, blackline, playbook, issues list, markup or negotiation, by a version token, by tracked-changes metadata, by a firm name, or by an entity pair. Its distinct default is a CLAUSE-REFERENCED NEGOTIATION APPARATUS over ONE named instrument whose party slots are already filled and whose execution block is still open - which is precisely what the schema default's matter-and-role pair does not describe, what `law_practice.precedent-bank` inverts (blank parties by design), what `law_practice.transactional-deal` refuses to hold (deal-level spine, not one instrument), and what `legal` cannot yet see (no completed execution block). It deliberately does NOT hold the deal-level working group list, steps plan, CP tracker, disclosure letter or insider list (`law_practice.transactional-deal`), the completion event and its delivery-status matrix (`law_practice.closing-binder`), the blank firm precedent (`law_practice.precedent-bank`), the dispute-ending offer exchange (`law_practice.settlement`), the live obligations under an already-executed contract (`business_operations.contract-administration`), or the executed and dated instrument itself (`legal`, on `legal`'s own evidence, and `legal` is a safety domain whose protection runs first). Declares no field rows and no folder dimensions under PR-6.

deterministic: PRECONDITION. These are activation signals only; the `law_practice` schema declares no field rows, so nothing here licenses a law_practice fact. Every accepted signal is a STRUCTURE plus a LABELLED SLOT, and this row's family test replaces the schema default's rather than repeating it: (i) a REPEATED INSTRUMENT STEM - a document title, short name or filename stem carried across two or more artefacts - PLUS (ii) at least one artefact whose own labelled slots are a CLAUSE-REFERENCED NEGOTIATION APPARATUS (comparison header naming two versions, issues-list columns keyed to clause numbers with side ownership and status, playbook position columns, deviation-approval columns, or a turn log with from-firm / to-firm / version). The schema's deletion test applies unchanged: strike every entity name and every document-type word, and if no comparison header, no clause-keyed column set and no position columns survive, nothing fires.

A DOCUMENT-COMPARISON or BLACKLINE HEADER, and it is this row's cleanest signal because no sibling produces it as its centre: a marked-up draft whose own comparison or revision metadata names TWO SOURCE VERSIONS of the same instrument (for example 'compared against v11 SC markup', 'blackline vs clean', or a document-comparison tool header naming Firm A Draft and Firm B Draft), together with a present-but-unexecuted signature or execution block and party slots that already carry real names rather than placeholders. Read through 00's text-document path, which yields "full text, headings, metadata, links, and structural information". The discriminating evidence is the TWO-VERSION COMPARISON STRUCTURE over one instrument, not the presence of tracked changes - tracked changes alone appear on pleadings, opinions, marketing decks and training scripts.

AN ISSUES LIST keyed to ONE instrument: a spreadsheet or table whose COLUMN SET pairs a clause or schedule cross-reference with an issue description, an OUR-POSITION or CLIENT-POSITION column, a COUNTERPARTY-POSITION or THEIR-POSITION column, a STATUS drawn from a small closed set (open, closed, parked, agreed, escalate), and frequently an OWNER or RESPONSIBLE-SIDE column. Read through 00's spreadsheet path - "Spreadsheets such as XLSX, XLS, CSV, TSV, ODS, and Numbers exports should yield workbook or file metadata, sheet names, column headers, visible cell values, table-like regions, formulas only when useful, and dates or identifiers from labeled cells". The discriminating evidence is the CLAUSE CROSS-REFERENCE plus the SIDE-OWNED POSITION pair: a deal CP tracker cross-references clauses too, but its rows are conditions of a transaction with satisfied/waived status, not bargaining positions on an instrument; a contract-administration register's rows are live obligations across many contracts.

A PLAYBOOK or POSITION MATRIX: a table or structured note whose COLUMN SET pairs a clause topic or playbook rule with POSITION columns - preferred, fallback, walkaway, approve-if, or equivalent closed labels - and often a rationale or authority column. The discriminating evidence is the POSITION GRAMMAR aimed at the DRAFTER or NEGOTIATOR, not at a bound party. A blank firm precedent's drafting notes instruct the drafter about optional clauses without encoding walkaway positions against a live counterparty; that is `law_practice.precedent-bank`'s. A playbook with filled party names in its header and position columns against a live negotiation is this row's.

A DEVIATION or APPROVAL MATRIX: one row per requested departure from the playbook, carrying a playbook-rule or clause reference, the requested deviation, a requester, an approver role, a decision, and a date. It is the governance layer over the playbook and is detected in order to be protected - it encodes which commercial concessions the client authorised - never in order to be moved.

A TURN or CIRCULATION LOG for ONE instrument: one row per negotiation turn carrying a turn number or date, a FROM-FIRM or FROM-SIDE slot, a TO-FIRM or TO-SIDE slot, a version stem, and often a delta or covering-note reference. The side-crossing circulation of successive versions of one instrument is the grouping spine; a firm email domain or a legal-sounding subject alone never fires.

AN EMAIL whose structured slots tie it to an already-evidenced instrument negotiation: a subject carrying the instrument stem plus a version or turn token, sender and recipient roles crossing a named side boundary, and a redline or issues-list attachment named in the message. Position is weighted for the reason 00 gives - a token in a filename, title or page-one heading is more meaningful than the same text in a reference list. A firm email domain, a source type, or a negotiation-sounding subject alone never fires.

AN ARCHIVE whose manifest, read WITHOUT unpacking because "the normal scan should never extract archive contents to the filesystem", shows member paths repeatedly encoding one instrument stem across clean, redline, issues-list and playbook families. Directory names are observations and become facts on no member.
needs_llm: DECIDING THE SIDE, inherited from the schema and worse here because both sides circulate near-identical redlines. Buyer markup and seller markup of the same SPA differ only in which comparison header and which issues-list OWNER column match the holder's own apparatus. Where the side is unresolved the model must abstain: "A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown."

Separating a practitioner-run negotiation from the holder's OWN contract being negotiated - the founder negotiating their own sale, the employee reviewing their own offer letter with counsel's redlines they received as client. The practitioner-side anchor is the schema's: an allocated matter reference belonging to the holder's firm, a time record, work product the holder produced. Absent that, this is `legal.personal-legal-matters` or career material and the row must abstain.

Separating a LEGAL negotiation from a CONSULTING or commercial markup of a statement of work. Scope, fees, confidentiality, deliverables, tracked changes and two-organisation signature blocks occur on both; explicit counsel or representation roles, a legal-services scope, a playbook with walkaway positions, or a clause-keyed issues list with side-owned legal positions carry the legal side. Where only the engagement paper exists, the honest outcome is Review Later.

Separating a LIVE negotiation draft from a KEPT precedent or a published model. Bracketed placeholders across all party positions with blank execution blocks are `law_practice.precedent-bank`'s; filled party names plus an open execution block plus comparison or issues apparatus are this row's. One leftover `[TBC]` in a schedule of an otherwise populated draft does not demote it to a precedent.

Deciding whether two instrument stems are one negotiation or two - a main agreement and its disclosure letter, an SPA and its tax deed, a master services agreement and a statement of work. Bridging by matching party names or clause text similarity is forbidden; only an exact cross-reference or user decision authorises multi-membership.
Reading unlabelled negotiation prose - a running-text summary of open points, a scanned marked-up page, a handwritten markup photographed then OCRed - where no column set exists to detect.

Abstaining whenever the instrument-stem-and-clause-apparatus pair cannot be cited: "Correct abstention is a successful outcome because the product’s goal is reliable organization, not maximum file movement."
never_alone: The words draft, redline, blackline, markup, playbook, issues list, negotiation, clean, compared, or tracked changes in a filename, title or folder. These are document-type and lifecycle words; the family's deletion test strikes them.

A VERSION TOKEN ALONE - v12, -final, -CLEAN, -REDLINE, Rev.C. 00 already treats version family as a universal file fact, and a version marker sits equally on pleadings, opinions, decks and training scripts.

TRACKED-CHANGES METADATA or a document-comparison tool producer name alone. Authoring tools write those slots on every kind of professional document; 00: "It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension".

AN ENTITY PAIR ALONE - two company names with or without registration numbers. Suppliers, litigants, landlord and tenant, payer and payee all appear as pairs. This row rests on a clause-referenced apparatus over one instrument, not on two named entities.

A LAW-FIRM, COUNSEL, CLIENT or COUNTERPARTY NAME ALONE, or any of them beside a document-type word. Read across from "A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization."
A CLAUSE, SCHEDULE or PARAGRAPH REFERENCE ALONE. An identifier supplies LINKAGE only after its own labelled role is established.

A CONFIDENTIAL, PRIVILEGED, SUBJECT-TO-CONTRACT, WITHOUT-PREJUDICE or COMMERCIALLY-SENSITIVE LABEL. The literal observation is preserved and no legal status is decided; such a label appears on commercial, HR and insurance documents constantly.
A SOURCE TYPE or EXTENSION ALONE, including text_document, spreadsheet, email, archive, image, ocr and every extension this row lists.
A FILENAME or FOLDER containing SPA, MSA, NDA, agreement, contract, deal, project or final. Paths stay local; a folder name is an unlabelled position.

DOWNLOAD-SESSION, THREAD, ARCHIVE or CURRENT-DIRECTORY MEMBERSHIP. 00: "A session should never be treated as proof of topic". A data-room bulk download of drafts is a session, not a negotiation group.

MATCHING PARTY NAMES, CLAUSE TEXT or SEMANTIC SIMILARITY ACROSS TWO INSTRUMENTS. Negotiation drafts are near-identical by drafting convention; similarity would bridge unrelated confidential negotiations. This is a privacy rule before it is an accuracy one.
PUBLIC AVAILABILITY of a form of agreement, a regulatory filing or a news report about the deal as proof that the local draft, the playbook or the issues list is low-sensitivity.
A PERSON'S NAME ALONE in any negotiator, approver or signatory role.

work_types: marked-up draft and blackline comparison of one instrument
clause-keyed issues list or open-points schedule
negotiation playbook with preferred, fallback and walkaway positions
deviation or exception approval matrix against a playbook
turn or circulation log for successive versions
covering note or markup email transmitting a redline turn
approval email or sign-off on a playbook deviation
archived negotiation pack of clean, redline, issues list and playbook members
grouping_reasons: ONE INSTRUMENT FROM FIRST MARKUP TO PRE-EXECUTION CLEAN, joined by the instrument stem plus the clause-referenced apparatus: the clean drafts, the blacklines, the issues list, the playbook, the deviation matrix and the turn log. Content-incoherent and purpose-coherent, which is 00's own licence - "The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent." The anchor supports candidate membership and copies no party, price, position or status fact onto any member.

ONE ISSUE THREAD INSIDE THAT INSTRUMENT, joined by an exact clause or schedule cross-reference repeated across an email, a marked-up extract, an issues-list row and a playbook rule. Internal fragments frequently omit the instrument stem, which is why the clause reference is admitted as linkage and struck as never-alone when it appears without one.

ONE VERSION FAMILY across sides: successive drafts of the same instrument, linked by an explicit document-comparison header naming its two source versions. 00 already treats membership of a version family as a universal fact, so `version_family` carries this without any law_practice field.

SPARSE MEMBERS JOIN WITHOUT INHERITING. A single marked-up schedule page, a scanned signature-block extract still showing blanks, or a short covering email may enter the candidate neighbourhood by an exact reference and still carry no instrument, party or position fact of its own. "It should not form a supported group when there is no valid anchor", and the converse holds: a valid anchor does not write itself onto its members.
NOT grouping reasons: shared party names across two instruments; shared practice area; a common firm name; a download session; semantic similarity of clause text.

template.why: EMPTY BY CONTRACT, for the schema's three reasons - no declared field to branch on under PR-6, no deep template unlocking from a safety co-activation since "Finance, identity, medical, and legal material should be implemented first as safety domains", and the disclosure cost of client and matter levels. WHERE THIS ROW'S PROSE RECOMMENDATION DIFFERS FROM THE SCHEMA'S, and it is a reason the row exists: the schema default recommends client (only where multi-client and approved), then matter, then document function, then period. HERE THE FIRST ORGANISING TOKEN IS THE INSTRUMENT STEM, then the ISSUE or CLAUSE THREAD, then the version or turn. An issues-list row, a playbook rule and a blackline are unintelligible without the instrument they belong to - 00's own argument is "A work type such as Homework 3 is meaningful only after the course is known". The instrument stem is still seeded destination-INELIGIBLE whenever it embeds a client or counterparty name (an SPA titled with both parties discloses the negotiation's existence); a neutral short name or matter-scoped alias is the only candidacy worth offering, and only with explicit user approval. A NAMED THIRD PARTY - counterparty, beneficial owner named in a schedule, individual signatory - may NEVER be a folder level. NOT TIME-FIRST: circulation time, document date, approval date and filesystem time mean different things, and "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." Whatever lands stays a recommendation: "The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions."

Reciprocal already on that row. If R1c judges the split too fine, one row folds - see NJ-CN-1. Provenance: inference.

Blank party and execution slots plus drafting notes are the neighbour's inverse-recognition signal; filled party names plus an open execution block plus comparison or issues apparatus are this row's. falls_through_to.why: Principal fallback for a stray blackline, issues list, playbook or deviation matrix when no accepted instrument group is active. These encode counterparty names and bargaining positions about someone who may never have chosen this filesystem. 00: "Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts." Also: "Rare but sensitive files such as passports, visas, and legal documents may be surfaced as protected records even when they do not meet a normal group-size threshold."

Readable negotiation-shaped artefacts whose SIDE or legal-versus-consulting character is unresolved. 00: "Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision."

Password-protected negotiation packs and proprietary comparison binaries. 00 names "Unsupported or Encrypted may hold" for unreadable and encrypted material, and separately: "Password-protected, malformed, nested, or oversized archives should be marked as unreadable or partially inspected rather than forced open".

Published model agreements, textbook markup exercises without training marks, and form libraries with no firm-playbook apparatus. 00: "Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association."

A standalone clean draft with no comparison header, no issues list and no matter neighbourhood. 00: "Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group."

A positively evidenced screen capture of an e-sign envelope or portal whose OCR does not establish an accepted instrument neighbourhood. 00: "Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship."

sensitivity_why: Strictest posture available at this row, and it is a leg of the node test this row passes distinctly rather than by inheritance alone. FIRST, the corpus sentence in 00 names legal records inside a highly personal collection, and a negotiation pack routinely also carries counterparty identity, pricing and private correspondence. SECOND, playbooks and issues lists encode BARGAINING POSITIONS - walkaway lines, approved deviations, side-owned concessions - whose disclosure can harm a client even when no third-party witness list is present; that is a posture the schema default argues from third-party exposure, and this row extends it to STRATEGY EXPOSURE before any instrument is executed. THIRD, existence is disclosive: a visible folder named for a counterparty and an SPA announces that a deal is being negotiated. 00's UI point lands here: "A summary such as “11 protected identity records” may be safe to show, while a visible list of passport filenames on a shared screen may not be."
